name: Newcastle University

settingEvidence.evidence: Bring a school group to experience our city centre campus and learn about university life.

fees.text: £10,050 per year for Home (UK) students on full-time undergraduate courses starting in 2027 (2027/28). Newcastle says fees for 2028/29 have not been confirmed (it suggests they could be £10,320 at the same rate of increase). A significant fee reduction applies to a work placement or study abroad year.

livingCosts.text: Rent in University-owned or managed partnership accommodation (bills included) is about £543-£924 a month for undergraduates. Newcastle's rough monthly guide also lists groceries about £144, socialising about £99 and a SIM-only phone about £16 (compiled August 2025; the academic year is not stated).

source.evidence: Rent in University-owned or managed partnership accommodation (includes bills, such as electricity, water, gas and wifi): Undergraduate: £543– £924, Postgraduate: £392 – £940

openDays.text: Next undergraduate open day: Saturday 21 November 2026, 9:00-16:00 (the booking form lets you choose 2027 or 2028 as your year of entry). No later dates are listed yet.

source.evidence: Saturday 21 November 2026

contextual.summary: Applicants who meet one or more contextual criteria may get an offer up to two grades below the typical entry requirements, with no separate application.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to two grades below the typical entry requirements

criteria.detail: Your home postcode is in POLAR4 Quintile 1 or 2: a neighbourhood with a low rate of progression to higher education. Newcastle has a postcode checker.
You have experienced any time in care during your life.

You are estranged from your family and no longer have support due to a breakdown in that relationship (this may include biological, adoptive or step-parents, or other family members who previously provided support).
You are eligible for free school meals. If you attend an independent school but would have been eligible in the state sector, you may also qualify (checked with data supplied by UCAS).
You have sole or shared responsibility for the care of a relative because they are ill, have a disability, are experiencing mental distress, or are affected by substance abuse.
You attend a state school in North East England (Regional Contextual Offer).

contextual.rulesText: You may be eligible if you meet one or more of the criteria. There is no separate application: make sure the relevant information is in the 'Applicant Context' section of your UCAS application. Eligibility for a contextual offer does not guarantee that an offer will be made.

source.evidence: Eligible applicants may receive an offer of up to two grades below the typical entry requirements.

programmes.name: PARTNERS Programme (Supported Entry Route)
programmes.summary: A widening-access route for Year 13 applicants: a lower offer (up to three A level grades lower), a free Academic Summer School and support from application to enrolment.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 13 (or equivalent) applicants who live in the UK, pay Home fees, do not already hold a higher education qualification, are predicted at least CCC and meet at least one eligibility criterion. You apply after submitting your UCAS application; students now in Year 12 apply next year.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Essential: UK resident; Home fee status; no existing higher education qualification; predicted CCC or above (or, if grades are already achieved, they must meet the lower PARTNERS offer). Plus at least one of: a low-progression or deprived home postcode (IMD, ACORN or TUNDRA); attending a low-performing school or college (for example GCSE Attainment 8 of 44 or less, or over 50% of pupils on free school meals); an ethnic group under-represented at Newcastle; free school meals, Pupil Premium or discretionary hardship payments; time in care; neither parent/carer holding a degree; a disability or long-term health condition with PIP at the required level; recognised carer; estranged; family armed forces service; Gypsy, Roma or Traveller; refugee, asylum seeker or humanitarian protection; parent/carer of a child under 17; or extenuating personal circumstances. These are the 2027-entry criteria and can change each year.
benefits: Lower offer: up to three A level grades lower than the typical offer (Newcastle's example: AAA becomes BBB), if you complete the Academic Summer School and make Newcastle your firm choice
Free PARTNERS Academic Summer School (PASS) in the summer before you start
Dedicated support from application to enrolment
programmes.offerReduction: Up to three A level grades (or equivalent) lower than the typical offer
programmes.subjects: All subjects (the summer school strand matches your firm-choice course)

notes: All six courses use 2027 entry: each course page says its requirements and offers apply to 2027 entry (start September 2027). No 2028-entry pages are published yet.

No course page names an admissions test and Newcastle is not on UAT-UK's TMUA list for 2027 entry. Mathematics and Economics (GL11) accepts grade 2 in any STEP paper as an alternative to a second listed A level.

Economics, Economics and Finance, Economics and Business Management and Finance share the same headline offer (AAB excluding General Studies); Politics and Economics is AAB with General Studies accepted; Mathematics and Economics needs an A in Mathematics.

Alternative offers (access-schemes page): contextual, Regional Contextual, High Performance Athlete and Realising Opportunities are each up to 2 grades lower; PARTNERS is up to 3 grades lower. Pathways to Newcastle (up to 2 grades lower) covers science, maths and engineering courses only.

Regional offers apply only to people who live or study in the North East or Tees Valley: a Regional Guaranteed Offer for eligible postcodes and a Regional Contextual Offer (up to two grades lower) for state-school students in the region; both need predicted CCC or above and the course's subject requirements.

Opportunity Scholarships (cash bursaries, awarded automatically by household income): £2,000 a year (up to £25,000), £1,250 (£25,001-£35,000), £750 (£35,001-£40,000). The page does not say which year these amounts apply to.

Campus postcode NE1 4SE is the Business School (5 Barrack Road), where the economics and finance courses are taught; the University's main postal address is NE1 7RU. Newcastle also runs Experience Days (Years 12 and 13) for school groups, not researched.
